note: The INTEGRATION layer game.js:2352-2637 `_tick()` is ported in full structurally: the exact stage order (ground probe / on-foot / boarding / flying / crashed, then combat+fx, boundary+zones, autosave, engine+hood, wind+world, HUD+targets), reproduced as named RunStage() calls that record LastStageOrder for GameLoopProbe.cs to read back as proof, not a claim. Also ported: _setupInput's key bindings this file owns (Enter/Tab/V/C/X/Z/Cmd-tap/F/M/H/Escape/Space/1-0 -- flying's stick stays in FlightInput.cs, reused not duplicated), resetPlane/igniteEngine/stopEngine/seatEmpty (697-760), a condensed swapToPlane (774-832), ownPlaneTargets (844-848), a minimal target registry (register/cycle/pickAt, target.js's selection half -- the card/paint half is UI.Target.TargetCardView, already ported elsewhere), saveState's shape (1043-1095, condensed), and the engine/hood invariant (2544-2620). The plane board/exit climb sequence (foot.js:649-1032) is ported here on purpose: FootController.cs's own header explicitly cuts it as belonging to 'the Flight/Cockpit system, already a separate port unit' -- that unit is this file. NOT ported, each a named public hook instead of a silent gap: cinema.js (no counterpart exists anywhere), CityRenderer's per-frame world.update (another agent is writing CityRenderer.cs concurrently), Guns/Rockets/BulletSim/ImpactFx/PlaneDamage/Blast/BreakingGlass construction (GameLoop supplies the ORDER via a List<ITickable>, not the IDamageWorld/IBallisticsWorld wiring, which belongs to whoever owns CombatWorldHooks.cs), CrashSequence/AirframeBreakup construction (a Func<PlaneController,CrashSequenceHandle> factory hook), the warn-grid fullscreen overlay, the _keepCameraOutside dolly-clamp, world.spawn-point lookup (SPAWN_YAW fallback), Pickups, goAirport/_parkInShed (ShedLayout-dependent, not wired), and the seated-pose leg bend (characters.js:1991-2266 setSeated -- CharacterRig.cs cites those lines but does not implement them; this file freezes the existing pose at the seat via CharacterRig.FreezePose/RestoreFrozen instead, which is the documented gap, not a silent one).

Startup FLOW and DATA: the auth round-trip (register/login/me, delegating to the already-ported NetClient+TokenStore, main.js:63-251), the hero roster (validHeroes's race-migration and hid-minting, main.js:148-170; create/select/delete hero, main.js:371-609; a PlayerPrefs-backed local mirror of main.js's tf-chars-<user> localStorage key), entering the world (startFlight, main.js:661-720 -- wires a PlaneController + spawns a CharacterRig body + applies a condensed _applyResume), leaving/logout (main.js:762-818, same order: save-then-flush-then-clear-token, and logout touches ONLY the session token per the JS's own comment), and the boot IIFE (main.js:838-856: a live token reopens straight to the character screen, never auto-logs-out on reload, '-autostart' command-line flag standing in for '?auto=1' since a compiled build has no URL -- and is never persisted, matching main.js:821-824's own requirement). Race -> starter-plane mapping is role-based (veggie=DPS, toys=TANK) per the project's own 'no plane picking on the personage screen' rule. NOT ported: the actual login-form and WoW-style race-card creation SCREENS (DOM/CSS in the JS, main.js:257-526) -- no UI.Boot/UI.Character views exist yet (the brief's ported UI/* list is Hud/Target/SkillBar/Settings/Map only), so every screen action is a public method here (SubmitAuth/SelectHero/CreateHero/...) plus events (ScreenChanged/RosterChanged/AuthError) for a future view to bind to, the same 'feed an existing view' pattern GameLoop.cs uses for HUD/Target/SkillBar.
